title: Longitudinal melanonychia as a presenting sign of nail unit squamous cell carcinoma: A case series and narrative review
abstract: Background: Nail unit squamous cell carcinoma (nSCC) presenting as longitudinal melanonychia is underrecognized, particularly among patients with skin of color (SOC). This review identifies patient, tumor, and human papillomavirus (HPV) characteristics. Summary: A review from peer-reviewed articles plus five institutional cases yielded 59 total cases. The majority (69.6%) were male, with a median age of 53 years. Among those with known Fitzpatrick Skin Type or race, 86.9% had SOC. Fingernails accounted for 87.7% of tumors. Longitudinal melanonychia was the only finding in 23.7% of cases, while hyperkeratosis, onychodystrophy, and verrucous changes were reported in 30.5%, 18.6%, and 15.3% of cases, respectively. The lateral nailfold was involved in 80.6% of cases. Most (81.4%) tumors were in situ at diagnosis. When performed, HPV testing was positive in 76.0% of cases, with high‑risk types (including HPV 16, 56, 58, and 59) predominating (76.9%). Key Messages: nSCC should be considered in the differential of longitudinal melanonychia, especially in patients with SOC over age 40 and a history of HPV infection presenting with lateral nailfold involvement, hyperkeratosis, onychodystrophy, or verrucous changes. Recognizing these findings may reduce diagnostic delay and allow earlier, tissue‑sparing treatment.

title: MedMCP: An Open Agentic Ecosystem for Medical Imaging Workflows
abstract: Abstract Deep learning has driven rapid progress in medical image analysis, with methods for tasks such as organ segmentation, anomaly detection, and radiology report generation now matching or surpassing expert performance on several benchmarks. While many methods are released as open source, their routine adoption by clinicians and medical researchers remains limited. The bottleneck is not a lack of capable tools, but the absence of infrastructure to make them accessible to non-technical users. To break this barrier, we present MedMCP , an agentic framework that solves this last-mile problem along two axes: (1) a local agentic workspace that lets users apply state-of-the-art image analysis methods through natural language, and (2) a community-driven tool ecosystem that lets developers deploy and distribute capabilities as validated, independently testable servers. MedMCP enforces a strict orchestration-execution boundary in which a local language model translates user intent into workflow plans, while all image analysis is delegated to domain-specific tools. The framework runs entirely on-premise, every side-effecting operation passes through a human-in-the-loop permission gate, and a full provenance trail links each output to the tools, parameters, and inputs that produced it. An inspectable workspace lets users verify intermediate results rather than blindly trusting the agent, and completed sessions distill into deterministic, shareable workflows that re-execute without the agent, turning one-off interactions into reproducible analyses. This paper introduces the project’s general idea and describes the design principles that guide its development. Beyond a single toolkit, we envision MedMCP as a community-driven platform where each contributed tool becomes easily accessible, compounding individual efforts into shared capability. https://medmcp.ai https://github.com/medmcp

title: TPTBox: Torso Processing ToolBox
abstract: The Torso Processing ToolBox (TPTBox) is a Python package for processing BIDS-compliant medical imaging datasets (CT, MRI), with a focus on torso and spine analysis. It provides NIfTI I/O, reorientation and resampling, Points of Interest computation for vertebrae, 2D and 3D snapshots, registration, stitching, and segmentation integrations.

title: Abstract B040: Learning multimodal breast cancer phenotypes for precision oncology
abstract: Abstract Background: Screening mammography is the cornerstone of breast cancer detection and is routinely performed before treatment initiation, providing a unique opportunity for early risk stratification. Beyond tumor detection, screening mammograms contain imaging biomarkers that reflect underlying tumor biology and the surrounding breast microenvironment. However, treatment response and long-term outcomes are driven by complex interactions between imaging phenotypes and patient-specific clinical characteristics that are not fully captured by mammography or conventional clinicopathologic staging alone. Integrating pre-treatment mammograms with longitudinal clinical data enables comprehensive patient representations that can inform therapeutic decision-making before neoadjuvant therapy (NAC) begins. Methods: We developed a multimodal framework to learn comprehensive patient phenotypes by integrating pre-treatment mammograms with longitudinal unstructured multispecialty clinical notes. Mammograms were encoded using MammoFM, a federated breast imaging foundation model pre-trained on large-scale, multi-institutional datasets, with the four standard views (CC and MLO) fused through a multi-view attention mechanism. Longitudinal peri-diagnostic EHR notes (3 months before to 2 months after diagnosis) were processed using a large language model (LLM) to generate semantic clinical embeddings from key patient characteristics. Imaging and clinical embeddings were then integrated through a cross-modal fusion transformer to learn unified multimodal patient phenotypes that capture complementary imaging and clinical information. These transferable phenotypic representations were subsequently leveraged for downstream prediction of pathological complete response (pCR) following NAC and long-term distant recurrence risk. Results: The multimodal phenotyping framework was developed using an internal cohort of 1,064 breast cancer patients from Mayo Clinic (AZ, MN, and FL) and evaluated on an independent held-out test set (n = 35). The learned multimodal patient representations consistently outperformed unimodal approaches across downstream prediction tasks. For long-term recurrence prediction, the multimodal phenotype achieved 85.71% balanced accuracy and an AUROC of 0.760, compared with 71.43% accuracy for mammography-only and 78.57% for clinical-only models. For prediction of pCR, the multimodal phenotype achieved 64.29% accuracy, outperforming mammography-only (35.71%) and clinical-only (46.43%) models. Conclusions: We developed a transferable multimodal patient phenotyping framework that integrates pre-treatment mammography with longitudinal clinical documentation to learn comprehensive representations of breast cancer patients. These multimodal phenotypes consistently outperformed imaging- or clinical-only representations for predicting pCR and long-term recurrence, demonstrating their potential as a generalizable foundation for precision oncology, risk stratification, and personalized treatment planning. Citation Format: Xiaoyang Wei, Madhu Sikha, Zhemin Zhang, Judy W. Gichoya, Imon Banerjee. Learning multimodal breast cancer phenotypes for precision oncology [abstract]. In: Proceedings of the 19th AACR Conference on the Science of Cancer Health Disparities; 2026 Oct 18-21; Atlanta, GA. Philadelphia (PA): AACR; Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2026;35(10 Suppl):Abstract nr B040.

title: Deep Auxiliary Learning via Bilevel Feature Optimization for Label-Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Auxiliary learning (AL), which can improve the performance of a primary task by leveraging related auxiliary tasks, is commonly regarded as a special case of multi-task learning. Existing AL approaches typically require manually annotated auxiliary labels, increasing annotation costs, particularly in medical imaging where expert labeling is expensive. In this work, we investigate whether segmentation performance can be improved using auxiliary tasks whose labels are automatically derived from existing segmentation annotations, requiring no additional manual labeling. To address this, we propose a novel auxiliary learning framework, formulated as a bilevel optimization problem. Our method enables effective knowledge transfer between tasks via a feature communication module, enhancing the primary segmentation task. We evaluate the method on three medical image segmentation benchmarks under limited-label settings. The results demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior label efficiency. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/FupingWu90/ALBO.

title: Distribution-Based Regularization for Reward Fine-Tuning Diffusion and Flow Models
abstract: Reward fine-tuning is an effective way to adapt pretrained diffusion and flow-matching models to downstream objectives, but aggressive optimization often leads to mode collapse and distributional drift. Existing methods attempt to control this drift with reverse-KL regularization, implemented as an $\ell_2$ penalty on the velocity field; however, this functions by indirectly constraining sampling dynamics rather than directly acting on the generated distribution. To address this, we propose DFR (Distributional Functional Rewards), which augments the task reward with a distribution-dependent, per-sample reward that acts explicitly on the generated distribution. Formally, we generalize the KL-regularized objective from expected rewards, which are linear in the model's distribution, to convex functionals of it. The first variation of this objective defines an effective, distribution-dependent reward that directly penalizes deviation from the pretrained distribution. This formulation yields additive per-sample rewards for the Fréchet distance (FD), maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), and DreamSim diversity, recovering several recently proposed rewards as special cases. Across various text-to-image fine-tuning tasks, DFR matches the peak reward of KL-tuned baselines while increasing diversity by up to 29% at equal or lower drift.

title: A Central Limit Theorem for Intrinsic Fréchet Means on Real Grassmannians
abstract: Subspace-valued data arise in dimension reduction, image-set and video recognition, and signal processing, and the Fréchet mean is their standard sample mean [11,9,15,23]. We establish a central limit theorem for the intrinsic sample Fréchet mean of i.i.d. observations on the real Grassmann manifold $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$, as a specialization of the general theorem of [18]. Unlike prior results which require the distribution to vanish or place negligible mass near the cut locus of the population mean, we allow a continuous, possibly positive density. To enable our results, we derive two properties of $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$: the first is that the union of the cut loci of all points within distance $δ$ of the mean has volume $O(δ)$. The second is that the Hessian of the squared distance function is integrable. We also give a smooth density on $\mathrm{Gr}(1,2)$ for which the mean is unique but the Fréchet Hessian vanishes.

title: Adaptive federated ensemble learning with hyperparameter optimization for distributed healthcare IoT
abstract: The rapid evolution of IoT-enabled healthcare systems has resulted in large-scale distributed data generation across various institutions. While federated learning enables collaborative model training without centralized data, it degrades non-identical data distributions and statistical imbalance across clients. Moreover, the convergence instability and hyperparameter sensitivity remain critical challenges in heterogeneous healthcare environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Stability-Aware Secure Federated Ensemble Framework integrated with LampyraCetacea Optimization (ASEFE-LCO). The platform integrates FedAvg and FedProx algorithms with an adaptive multi-model ensemble mechanism to ensure convergence stability under non-IID conditions. To enhance predictive robustness, LampyraCetacea Optimization is employed for dynamic hyperparameter adaptation in non-convex environments. To offer formal privacy tamper-proof protection, an integrated blockchain layer is applied to ensure decentralized auditability. The proposed architecture offers an end-to-end intelligent platform that combines optimization stability, security assurance, scalability, and distributed knowledge integration. As a core tenet of the proposed model, the experimental evaluation of the IoT healthcare security benchmark dataset achieves 99.94% accuracy, indicating a robust, secure, and clinically interpretable solution for an intelligent healthcare system.

title: Forest Floor Biodiversity Benchmark Image Dataset
abstract: The dataset comprises 5,523 frames at 1920 × 1080 resolution (Full HD, 1080p), documenting forest floor environments in forested areas surrounding Warsaw, Poland. The dataset was collected using two smartphone devices: the Xiaomi Poco X5 and Apple iPhone 16. The images capture natural forest floor features, including fallen leaves, pine needles, moss, lichens, twigs, deadwood, exposed soil, small plants, and other organic materials. The collection represents the visual diversity of forest ground surfaces and vegetation under naturally occurring environmental and lighting conditions. Images were acquired using smartphone cameras, providing variations in color reproduction, sharpness, texture detail, and image characteristics between devices. All frames have a Full HD resolution of 1920 × 1080 pixels, supporting detailed visual analysis and consistent image processing. The dataset is suitable for computer vision research, forest floor classification, ecological image analysis, vegetation and ground-cover identification, biodiversity-related studies, and the development and evaluation of machine learning and deep learning models. The files .0** are split regular ZIP archive for easier download. Please download all the files first. If you're on linux, please use zip -s 0 FILENAME OF DOWNLOADED FILE --out joint.zip; then unzip joint.zip. If you're on windows, please use Winrar, 7zip or similar app.

title: Spatial localization of RNAs within the breast tumor microenvironment may affect progression and recurrence of DCIS
abstract: Abstract Background Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is a cancerous growth of breast duct cells that may remain indolent or progress to invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). As screening rates increase, the prevalence of DCIS diagnosis has risen with many women undergoing aggressive treatment with surgery, radiation, and endocrine therapy when diagnosed with DCIS. It is critical to identify factors that predict progression to invasive disease for improved outcomes. Studies involving the breast tumor microenvironment (TME) provide potential understanding of crosstalk between tumor epithelium and stroma to identify factors that influence progression of DCIS lesions. Methods To identify such biomarkers of breast cancer progression, we examined the TME using breast tissue microarrays (TMAs) representing matched benign (normal adjacent), DCIS, and IDC samples. We examined 139 cores which provided data from 47 unique patients. We characterized the expression and spatial distribution patterns of regulatory RNAs (mRNAs and long-noncoding RNAs) including Runt-related transcription factor 1 (RUNX1), Runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2), Mitotically activated long non-coding RNA (MANCR), Cluster of Differentiation 90 (CD90), C-X-C motif chemokine 12 (CXCL12), C-X-C chemokine receptor type 6 (CXCR6), and tumor protein 63 (TP63), using RNAScope fluorescence in situ hybridization (RNA-FISH) and a panel of stromal marker proteins (i.e., Cluster of Differentiation 3 (CD3), Cluster of Differentiation 68 (CD68), Cluster of Differentiation 34 (CD34), Alpha Smooth Muscle Actin (aSMA) and TP63) using multiplex immunofluorescence (IF). Results We identified several temporal and spatial expression signatures of RNAs and/or proteins throughout breast cancer progression, both in the epithelial and stromal compartment of benign, DCIS or IDC lesions. Spatial proximity analysis to assess location of markers away from epithelial boundary or within the myoepithelial layer of these lesions identified significant association with clinical parameters including tumor recurrence status. Conclusions The finding that decreased myoepithelial continuity maybe protective against recurrence could help better patient stratification for immunotherapy. This work emphasizes the importance of spatial localization of markers in the breast cancer tumor microenvironment and their importance for clinical outcome.

title: QoS-Aware Secure Federated Intelligence for Biomedical Electronics and Medical Informatics in Wireless Health Monitoring Networks
abstract: Wireless Health Monitoring Networks (WHMNs) that utilize Biomedical Electronics (BMEs) are rapidly changing how medical information is gathered and used in contemporary Medical Informatics through providing ongoing, real-time, and remote assessment and monitoring of essential physiological parameters; including electrocardiogram (ECG), body temperature, blood oxygen saturation, and heart rate. A number of constraints can limit the practical implementation of WHMNs including: stringent Quality of Service (QoS) requirements; limited energy availability; network scalability limitations; and significant risks associated with the transfer of sensitive medical information via open wireless networks. While conventional centralized routing and learning based approaches provide the ability to route packets and learn network behavior they require high levels of communication, make the network vulnerable to cyber threats, and do little to protect the privacy of patients' data. This paper describes a QoS aware secure federated intelligence framework designed specifically for BME driven WHMNs. The proposed framework will include: (1) Decentralized Federated Learning to enable distributed intelligence among edge nodes; (2) Trust based QoS Aware Routing to enable reliable and energy efficient communication throughout the network; and (3) a Lightweight Blockchain-Assisted Mechanism to provide authentication, integrity, and tamper resistance to the network. In contrast to traditional federated learning where edge node models are aggregated into a central server model for processing, the proposed framework enables edge nodes to train their own local models on their own data and to share only encrypted model updates rather than raw biomedical data; thereby reducing communication costs and increasing patient data privacy protection. Simulation results show that the proposed framework outperform other state of the art WHMN protocols in terms of Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR); End-To-End Delay (E2ED); Residual Energy per Node (REPN); and Overall Network Lifetime (ONL). Additionally, the security analysis provided in this paper demonstrates the proposed framework's robustness against Insider Attacks, Data Manipulation Attacks, and Unauthorized Access Attacks. These findings indicate the strong feasibility of the proposed framework for next generation Intelligent Healthcare and Medical Informatics Applications.

title: A generalist model for diverse text-guided medical image synthesis
abstract: Deep learning requires extensive data to achieve robust performance. However, data availability is often restricted in medicine due to patient privacy concerns. Synthetic data from medical image generative models present a possible solution to these challenges. Unfortunately, many models are often task-specific or trained on private datasets, limiting scalability and reproducibility. To address this, we introduce MediSyn: an open-access, generalist, text-guided latent diffusion model. MediSyn can generate images across 6 medical specialties and 10 imaging modalities, while being trained exclusively on public data. Our study provides several key contributions using MediSyn. First, we demonstrate that a generalist model can generate images of comparable quality to task-specific models across multiple specialties. Second, we show that this generalist approach is more computationally efficient than a suite of task-specific models. Third, we establish that a generalist model can produce realistic, text-aligned images across visually and medically distinct modalities. Fourth, we empirically demonstrate that these synthetic images are visually distinct from real images used in training. Finally, we show that a generalist model can produce images that improve classifier performance in data-limited settings across multiple specialties. Altogether, our findings highlight the potential of generalist image generative models to accelerate medical algorithmic research and development.

title: Ultrashort Echo Time Magnetization Transfer MRI for Cortical Bone Collagen Assessment and Its Association With Mineralization in Type 1 Diabetes
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) increases fracture risk beyond bone mineral density (BMD), implicating matrix quality. Whether ultrashort echo time magnetization transfer (UTE-MT) MRI can track collagen alterations in T1DM and their associations with mineralization is unknown. PURPOSE: To evaluate UTE-MT-derived magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) for monitoring in vivo cortical collagen alterations in T1DM and to investigate its associations with mineralization and multiscale bone properties. STUDY TYPE: Longitudinal animal model. ANIMAL MODEL: 18 male New Zealand white rabbits (Age: 5-6 months) randomized to diabetic (n = 12) and control (n = 6) groups. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T/3D gradient-echo UTE-MT sequence. ASSESSMENT: UTE-MT MRI was performed at baseline (week 0) and weeks 12, 16, and 20 post-alloxan induction. Cortical MTR was calculated from paired MT-on/off images and quantified over cortical regions of interest. Reference measurements at the terminal time point (week 20) included micro-CT (cortical porosity [CtPo]), histomorphometry (mineral apposition rate [MAR], bone formation rate [BFR/BS]), fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) (collagen cross-linking), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) (hydroxyproline [Hyp]), histology (collagen maturation), and mechanical testing. STATISTICAL TESTS: The t-tests/Mann-Whitney U for endpoint cross-sectional comparisons, linear mixed-effects model for longitudinal MTR, Pearson correlations (r) for associations; p < 0.05 was considered significant. RESULTS: Cortical MTR declined in T1DM rabbits, becoming significantly lower than controls at week 12 and lowest at week 20. At termination, T1DM group demonstrated significantly higher CtPo (1.345 ± 0.270% vs. 0.591 ± 0.233%), elevated NE-xLR, reduced MAR, BFR/BS, Hyp, ECR, and collagen maturation (1.705 ± 0.548 vs. 5.474 ± 1.455). Mechanical properties (elastic modulus [E], yield strength [YS], toughness) were significantly lower in the T1DM group, with reductions of 44.1%, 35.2%, and 63.2% relative to controls, respectively. MTR at week 20 correlated positively with Hyp, ECR, collagen maturation, mineralization, and mechanical parameters (r = 0.562 to 0.900), and negatively with NE-xLR via partial correlation (r = -0.616) and CtPo (r = -0.826). DATA CONCLUSIONS: UTE-MT-derived MTR enables in vivo tracking of cortical collagen dynamics in T1DM. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 1. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

title: Deep learning–accelerated contrast-enhanced 3D MRI for acute optic neuritis: faster acquisition and improved lesion conspicuity
abstract: Objective To compare a deep learning-accelerated contrast-enhanced 3D T1-weighted sequence (T1-CUBE-DLS) with standard parallel imaging-accelerated T1-CUBE for detecting acute optic neuritis (ON). Methods This prospective study enrolled 59 patients with suspected acute ON (38 females; mean age 41.2 ± 12.8 years). All underwent contrast-enhanced whole-brain 3.0 T MRI including both T1-CUBE-DLS and standard T1-CUBE sequences. Two blinded neuroradiologists independently scored motion artifacts, subjective noise, and optic nerve clarity. Consensus readings recorded enhancement laterality, involved segments, and visual conspicuity. Enhancement length was measured per optic nerve, with inter-observer reliability assessed via intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland–Altman analysis. Clinical diagnosis by a senior neuro-ophthalmologist served as the reference standard. Results Acute ON was confirmed in 43 of 59 patients (72.9%). T1-CUBE-DLS reduced acquisition time by 36.2%. Subjective noise was equivalent between sequences ( p > 0.05), but T1-CUBE-DLS showed significantly fewer motion artifacts and superior optic nerve clarity (both p < 0.05). No significant difference was detected in diagnostic performance between the two sequences: sensitivity (88.4% vs. 86.0%), specificity (93.8% vs. 93.8%), and accuracy (89.8% vs. 88.1%; all p > 0.05). T1-CUBE-DLS demonstrated stronger visual conspicuity ( p = 0.011) and slightly longer measured enhancement length (mean difference, 0.836 mm; p < 0.0001). ICC for length measurement was 0.91 for T1-CUBE-DLS vs. 0.83 for standard T1-CUBE, with narrower 95% limits of agreement (−1.37 to 1.51 mm vs. − 3.1 to 2.4 mm). Conclusion T1-CUBE-DLS reduces acquisition time by 36.2%, with no significant difference in diagnostic accuracy detected, while improving enhancement conspicuity and measurement reproducibility, supporting its potential as a practical and efficient alternative for ON evaluation.

title: Multiclass Prediction of Stroke-Hypertension Comorbidity Using Soft Voting Ensemble with SMOTE Evaluation: A National Stroke Hospital Study in Sumatra
abstract: Hypertension and stroke represent a critical comorbidity pair with a substantial global health burden. This study formulated their joint risk assessment as a four-class multiclass classification problem using clinical data from 100 patients at the National Stroke Hospital, West Sumatra. A soft voting ensemble integrating logistic regression, K-nearest neighbor, and random forest classifiers was developed and evaluated with and without synthetic minority oversampling technique. The soft voting ensemble demonstrated the most stable predictive performance across both evaluation settings, achieving an accuracy of 80.0%, a macro F1-score of 82.6%, and an area under the curve of 92.7% with synthetic minority oversampling technique. However, applying synthetic minority over-sampling technique yielded no meaningful improvement over the non-oversampled scenario. McNemar's test confirmed that the soft voting ensemble significantly outperformed logistic regression (p = 0.031) but was statistically equivalent to non-linear models. Feature importance analysis consistently identified age and cholesterol as the dominant predictors, supporting established evidence on age-related vascular deterioration and atherosclerotic risk. These findings suggest that the soft voting ensemble provides a stable framework for multiclass comorbidity prediction and may support earlier risk stratification in clinical settings, though results should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size.

title: Human-in-the-loop large language model framework for identification of cutaneous immune-related adverse events
abstract: This study evaluated a retrieval-augmented, multi-agent large language model (LLM)–driven, human-in-the-loop framework for detecting cutaneous immune-related adverse events (cirAEs) from clinical notes. Compared with the unassisted manual-review group, the LLM-assisted group demonstrated higher accuracy (F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77) and inter-rater agreement measured by Cohen’s κ ( κ = 0.82 vs 0.50), and reported an approximately one-third shorter average review time. This framework pilots how LLMs can be applied to identify immune-related toxicities and, more broadly, support accurate, scalable, and transparent adverse event data extraction.

title: Design and Development of NeuroSphere PET: A Next-Generation 7-T MR-Compatible Dedicated Brain PET Scanner
abstract: PET is the most powerful imaging modality for studying neurotransmitters, receptors, and neuromodulation in humans, complementing the anatomic and hemodynamic information provided by MRI. However, PET temporal resolution remains constrained by sensitivity, limiting studies of fast, dynamic neurochemical processes. To address this gap, we are developing the Human Dynamic NeuroChemical Connectome, an imaging system integrating NeuroSphere PET, a novel ultra-high-sensitivity dedicated brain PET camera, with the Siemens Healthineers Magnetom Terra.X, a clinical 7-T MRI scanner. This article describes the design, engineering, and simulation-based performance estimation of NeuroSphere PET. Sensitivity maximization drove 2 core design choices: a partial spheric detector arrangement with a 32-cm inner diameter and 70% solid-angle coverage and the use of 26-mm lutetium oxyorthosilicate crystals for high stopping power (∼90% at 511 keV), coupled to silicon photomultipliers in a light-sharing, depth-of-interaction-capable configuration. The system comprises 872 detector blocks organized across 19 rings and 218 modules. At the detector level, measured performance includes energy resolution of approximately 11% full width at half maximum (FWHM), depth-of-interaction resolution of approximately 8 mm FWHM, and coincidence timing resolution of approximately 500 ps FWHM. System-level performance was evaluated using the ultrafast Monte Carlo PET simulator, accounting for realistic detector response, positron range, photon noncollinearity, and interdetector scatter. Sensitivity was estimated from a 30-cm uniform sphere, predicting a peak sensitivity of about 38% and a whole-brain average exceeding 25%. Spatial resolution and image quality were assessed through Derenzo phantom simulations evaluated at both the center of the field of view and 8 cm off-center, indicating that 1.6-mm structures can be resolved near the center of the field of view and that resolution of less than 2 mm can be maintained at the cortex. The system incorporates a 3-dimensional-printed MRI-compatible gantry, a dedicated 16-channel parallel transmit-receive radiofrequency head coil, and a custom radiofrequency shielding enclosure for simultaneous PET/MRI at 7 T. By targeting sensitivity an order of magnitude higher than that of commercial PET systems, NeuroSphere PET is expected to enable simultaneous neurochemical and hemodynamic studies with substantially improved spatiotemporal resolution, providing new insights into brain function and connectivity.

title: From Adults to Children: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Chest X-Ray Classification under Domain Shift
abstract: Foundation models have shown significant potential across diverse fields and have been applied to medical imaging, but their robustness across patient populations remains unclear. In this work, we investigate foundation models' ability to generalize from adult to pediatric chest X-ray classification. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first benchmark to compare multiple foundation models under a common adult-to-pediatric evaluation setting while also analyzing the effect of adaptation depth. We harmonize VinDr-CXR and PediCXR into a five-label classification task and evaluate six foundation models and two CNN baselines. All models are adapted using adult data only and tested in both the in-domain and pediatric domains using linear probing, partial fine-tuning, and full fine-tuning. The benchmark reveals a clear and consistent trend: all models suffer a substantial performance degradation when transferred from adult to pediatric data, with drops exceeding 10 percentage points. While Macro-AUROC values reach approximately 92% on the adult test set, performance decreases to around 78% on the pediatric domain. Another important finding is that increasing the depth of adaptation does not significantly improve cross-population generalization. Moreover, strong in-domain performance does not translate into better performance on pediatric data.

title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds. Purely LLM-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments. We propose DRAGO, a repair framework that replaces this ungrounded critique with deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis, and retains a rewrite only when the diagnosed error weight strictly decreases under a reference-free acceptance predicate. Across five benchmarks spanning logical reasoning (SMT-LIB2), constraint programming (MiniZinc), and planning (PDDL), DRAGO cuts regressions by nearly an order of magnitude, to 1.3%, while improving answer accuracy by 12.9 percentage points over zero-shot formalization and 8.7 percentage points over LLM-diagnostic repair, averaged across benchmarks. We also uncover two rendering defects in Planetarium that cause 50% (3,086 instances) of its floor-tile split to be inconsistent with the reference formalizations, and release a corrected split.

title: Comparison of G-CSF With and Without Plerixafor or Cyclophosphamide for Hematopoietic Stem-Cell Mobilization in Autologous Transplantation: A Retrospective Cohort Study (Preprint)
abstract: UNSTRUCTURED Background: Autologous hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) requires adequate peripheral blood stem-cell collection. The optimal mobilization regimen remains uncertain, particularly regarding the comparative effects of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) alone, G-CSF plus plerixafor, and G-CSF plus cyclophosphamide. This study compared cell-collection and short-term transplantation outcomes among patients undergoing autologous HSCT. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 80 patients with hematological malignancies who underwent autologous HSCT at the bone-marrow transplantation unit of Imam Khomeini Hospital, Urmia, Iran, between 2017 and 2022. Patients were classified according to mobilization regimen: G-CSF alone (n=23; 28.8%), G-CSF plus plerixafor (n=24; 30%), or G-CSF plus cyclophosphamide (n=33; 41.3%). Data were extracted from institutional transplantation records and archived medical records. Outcomes included CD34-positive cells, CD3 cells, total cells, admission-to-transplantation and transplantation-to-discharge intervals, neutrophil and platelet engraftment, and febrile days. Categorical and continuous variables were compared using Fisher’s exact test, one-way analysis of variance, and the Kruskal–Wallis test as appropriate; analyses were performed in SPSS version 20. Results: Age and sex distributions were not significantly different across regimens (p>0.05). Median CD34-positive cell count and CD34-positive percentage were highest with cyclophosphamide plus G-CSF, without significant differences (p=0.48 and p=0.35, respectively). Mean total cells were highest with plerixafor plus G-CSF (p=0.01), and median CD3 cell count was also highest with plerixafor plus G-CSF (p=0.009). Median neutrophil engraftment was 14 days (interquartile range [IQR], 11.50–26) with G-CSF alone and 11 days (IQR, 10–14) with plerixafor plus G-CSF (p=0.22). Admission-to-transplantation time differed significantly across groups, whereas transplantation-to-discharge time, platelet engraftment, and febrile days did not. Conclusion: In this single-center retrospective cohort, plerixafor plus G-CSF was associated with higher total-cell and CD3-related collection measures, while cyclophosphamide plus G-CSF yielded numerically higher CD34-related measures. Given nonsignificant differences in several clinical outcomes, these findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Photoacoustic-guided reflection-mode wavefront shaping through dynamic biological tissue
abstract: Strong optical scattering limits the depth at which light can be focused and used for imaging in biological tissue. Photoacoustic (PA)-guided wavefront shaping enables non-invasive light focusing in scattering media, but most existing implementations require optical and acoustic access from opposite sides of the sample and a rigidly aligned free-space optical path, which have confined these demonstrations to thin or static samples. Here, we combine a real-valued intensity transmission matrix (RVITM) algorithm with a photoacoustic guidestar (PA-RVITM) in a reflection-mode configuration. Modulated light is delivered through a flexible multimode fiber passing through the central aperture of a focused ultrasound transducer, enabling optical illumination and acoustic detection from the same side of the sample without a free-space combiner. Fiber integration preserved the wavefront shaping performance, and the reflection-mode PA-RVITM system achieved sub-second wavefront optimization with a ~14-fold PA signal enhancement through a diffuser. In ex vivo chicken breast tissue, the enhancement decreased with tissue thickness, reaching ~3.5 through a 2-mm chicken breast layer, with a speckle decorrelation time of ~450 ms. By performing an independent RVITM optimization at each scan position, our system enabled photoacoustic microscopy of a black nylon wire through the same layer, reducing the imaged line width from ~141 μm to ~102 μm, close to the nominal diameter of ~100 μm. This work advances PA-guided wavefront shaping toward a compact, same-side implementation for future biomedical therapeutic and imaging applications.

title: Defining and Generating Compositional Structure
abstract: Compositional structure is pervasive in nature and across scales: atoms combine into molecules, molecules into cells, and cells into organisms, while further compositional hierarchies appear within each level. More broadly, compositionality, the reuse and recombination of parts into novel structures, is a fundamental source of interesting complexity in both natural and artificial systems. Yet despite its importance, and despite our apparent ease in recognizing it, mathematical accounts capturing what we intuitively mean by compositional structure remain limited. Here, we fill this gap by formalizing a simple idea: compositional structure emerges when parts, considered together, reveal shared structure that is not captured when those parts are modeled separately. We express this idea using algorithmic information theory, the mathematics of information and compression, which provides a natural way to identify structure in arbitrary data without specifying in advance what that structure must look like. Applied across scales, our definition informs where and how compositional structure emerges within an object. Using tractable approximations, we then invert the framework to generate compositional objects: we specify the desired form of their compositional structure without prescribing their particular content, and optimize directly over strings and images. The resulting objects exhibit readily recognizable hierarchical reuse and part-whole organization, suggesting that the definition captures compositional structure rather than merely complexity, regularity, or shared information. Finally, we discuss implications for machine learning, including a new perspective on depth in neural architectures and principles for constructing compositional data curricula capable of supporting open-ended learning.

title: Intratumoral susceptibility signals in adult-type diffuse gliomas: associations with molecular profile, tumor grade, and overall survival
abstract: Purpose Intratumoral Susceptibility Signals (ITSS) are low-signal-intensity structures observed on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) which may reflect intratumoral microhemorrhages, calcifications, and neovascularization. Previous studies have demonstrated associations between ITSS, glioma grade, and molecular characteristics; however, their potential role in outcome prediction remains incompletely defined. This study investigated the diagnostic and and potential prognostic role of ITSS in adult diffuse gliomas. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 128 adult patients with histologically confirmed diffuse gliomas who underwent preoperative MRI including SWI. ITSS were graded from 0 to 3 according to the number of susceptibility signals. Associations between ITSS grade and CNS WHO tumor grade, IDH mutation status, MGMT promoter methylation and Ki-67 labeling index (LI) were evaluated. Overall survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Results ITSS grade was significantly associated with WHO glioma grade ( p < 0.001), with lower-grade tumors predominantly exhibiting ITSS grades 0–1 and higher-grade gliomas showing grades 2–3. IDH-mutant gliomas displayed significantly lower ITSS grades than IDH-wildtype tumors ( p < 0.001). ITSS grade was positively correlated with Ki-67 labeling index (Spearman's ρ = 0.423, p < 0.001). In the survival cohort ( n = 87) higher ITSS burden was significantly associated with shorter OS (ITSS 2–3 vs. 0–1: HR = 3.19, 95% CI 1.65–6.19; p < 0.001). However, this association was no longer significant after adjustment for established prognostic factors (HR = 1.40, 95% CI 0.69–2.86; p = 0.350), with IDH status emerging as the strongest independent association with shorter OS. Conclusion ITSS grading on SWI is associated with CNS WHO grade, molecular profile, proliferative activity, and OS in adult-type diffuse gliomas. Although ITSS was not an independent predictor of survival after adjustment for established prognostic factors, it may serve as a readily available, non-invasive imaging correlate of tumor aggressiveness, providing complementary information for preoperative tumor characterization while definitive molecular data are pending.

title: A hybrid scale attention network for uncertainty aware brain tumor MRI classification
abstract: Accurate and reliable classification of brain tumors from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is critical for timely clinical decision-making. Existing deep learning methods suffer from three key limitations: overconfident predictions without principled uncertainty estimates, lack of external validation across acquisition protocols, and parameter-heavy architectures unsuitable for resource-constrained deployment. To address these gaps, we propose Hybrid Scale-Attention Network, a lightweight framework comprising an EfficientNet-B3 backbone, a depthwise-separable Adaptive Multi-Scale Module (AMSM), and an Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) classification head. AMSM fuses three parallel dilated convolutional branches at rates {1, 2, 4} and an identity branch via learned softmax gating, forming a convex combination of multi-scale representations at an approximately 6.6× lower parameter cost than equivalent standard convolutions. The EDL head enables single-pass evidential uncertainty estimation based on Dirichlet strength. Through systematic four-variant ablation, we find that stacking a Dual Attention Module after AMSM degrades cross-dataset generalization despite modest in-domain gains, motivating its exclusion. On BRISC 2025, the proposed model achieves 99.20% accuracy and 99.30% macro-F1 with only 10.97 M parameters. Development-stage external validation on the PMRAM-BD cohort yields 97.41% accuracy without fine-tuning, indicating strong cross-dataset performance. Misclassified samples carry higher mean evidential uncertainty than correctly classified ones, with a misclassification detection AUROC of 0.9461 at single-pass inference cost (16.8 ms), offering an efficient alternative to MC-Dropout. Grad-CAM and UA-GradCAM visualizations alongside MSAD provide radiologist-interpretable localization and per-class scale-branch analysis. These results demonstrate that the proposed model offers a favorable trade-off among accuracy, parameter efficiency, and principled uncertainty quantification, supporting potential retrospective clinical investigation.

title: FedFound: Federated Foundation Model for GI endoscopy imaging
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is essential for identifying abnormalities and enabling early diagnosis, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and facilitating timely clinical intervention. While deep learning has shown promise in supporting GI diagnostics, most models require carefully labeled datasets that are costly to acquire and limited in scope. Foundation models offer a paradigm shift by learning general-purpose representations that can be adapted for diverse tasks, addressing data scarcity and variability. However, training such models on medical imaging data remains challenging due to privacy regulations, security concerns, and fragmented digital infrastructures that prevent centralized data aggregation, even as hospitals collectively generate vast amounts of endoscopic data. To overcome these barriers, we propose a federated learning (FL) framework for GI foundation models, allowing data to remain local while collaboratively training a shared model. We extensively evaluate multiple FL algorithms under both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings across three clinically relevant downstream tasks-classification, detection, and segmentation. We further evaluate our framework with a larger number of clients and across diverse pretraining strategies to assess its scalability and robustness. Our results demonstrate consistent performance gains, underscoring the potential of Federated Foundation Models to enable clinically validated AI applications and support secure, regulation-compliant deployment in real-world gastroendoscopy practice.

title: Bearing fault diagnosis based on ensemble empirical mode decomposition and t-distribution Quantum Particle Swarm optimized XGBoost
abstract: To improve the accuracy and robustness of bearing fault diagnosis in rotating machinery, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) and a t-distribution mutation Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization–optimized Extreme Gradient Boosting (tQPSO–XGBoost) model. First, EEMD is applied to decompose the collected vibration signals into several physically meaningful Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). Through correlation analysis, noise and interference components are removed, and the signals are reconstructed to highlight fault-related features. Then, typical time-domain and frequency-domain features are extracted from the reconstructed signals. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is employed for feature screening and dimensionality reduction to eliminate redundant information and enhance feature sensitivity. Finally, a t-distribution mutation strategy is introduced to improve the Quantum Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO) algorithm, which adaptively searches and optimizes the hyperparameters of the XGBoost model for intelligent recognition of bearing health states. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with conventional PSO–XGBoost, GWO–XGBoost, and standard XGBoost methods, the proposed EEMD–tQPSO–XGBoost method exhibits significant advantages in convergence speed, classification accuracy, and robustness. This study provides an efficient and stable solution for intelligent bearing fault diagnosis under complex working conditions.

title: The Impact of Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitors Combined with Panitumumab on Survival in RAS Wild-Type Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
abstract: A growing body of evidence suggests potential impact of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors on tumor biology and treatment response in colorectal cancer. However, it still remains to prove their impact on survival when used in combination with panitumumab in patients with RAS wild-type (KRAS/NRAS wild-type) metastatic colorectal cancer. This study aimed to assess the impact of ACE inhibitors (ACEIs) or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients receiving panitumumab. This retrospective cohort study included 122 patients with histopathologically proven RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer attending our clinics between January 2019 and April 2025. All patients had received first-line systemic chemotherapy. Patients were divided into two groups based on whether or not they received ACEI/ARB (users: n=52; non-users: n=70). PFS was defined as the time from the start of treatment until disease progression or death and OS was defined as the time from the start of treatment until death. The Kaplan–Meier method was used for survival analysis and prognostic factors were analyzed using univariate and multivariate Cox regression models. The median follow-up time was 58.9 (95% CI: 52.7–65.2) months. The median PFS was 16.32 (95% CI: 13.3–19.3) months in ACEI/ARB users and 10.97 (95% CI: 8.74–13.2) months in ACEI/ARB non-users (p=0.04). The median OS was 61.73 (95% CI: 54.5–68.9) months and 38.37 (95% CI: 28.7–47.9) months, respectively (p=0.018). The multivariate analysis demonstrated a significant association between ACEI/ARB usage and overall survival (HR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.27–0.81; p=0.008). A subgroup analysis did not show a statistically significant difference between ACEIs and ARBs. ACEI/ARB usage was found to be associated with longer progression-free survival and overall survival in patients with RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer. These data indicated that renin-angiotensin system inhibitors might play a potential role in tumor biology and treatment response. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these data in order to introduce them into clinical practice.

title: Estimating the eligible population for amyloid-targeting monoclonal antibody therapy in memory clinics: Application to lecanemab in France
abstract: Lecanemab was the first amyloid-targeting monoclonal antibody approved by the European Commission for treating patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease (AD). While this marketing authorization led to heterogeneous situations across European countries, France declined reimbursement, citing limited clinical benefit and concerns about the healthcare system's capacity to implement this new care pathway. This capacity depends directly on the number of eligible patients, yet robust estimates remain limited and highly variable across studies. Our objective was therefore to estimate the population eligible for lecanemab in France. Using transportability methods based on inverse odds of selection weighting, we articulated the nationwide consultation data from the French National Alzheimer Database (BNA) with the deeply phenotyped MEMENTO clinical cohort. Eligibility for lecanemab followed the French appropriate use recommendations: 1) clinical eligibility (age 50-90 years, MCI with common AD phenotype or mild AD dementia, MMSE ≥22), 2) biological eligibility (amyloid confirmation determined sequentially using plasma p-tau217, cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers and amyloid-PET), 3) absence of contraindications (APOEε4 homozygosity, anticoagulant use, MRI risk markers for ARIA). Among patients consulting French memory clinics, 19.5% met clinical eligibility criteria. Of these, 73.0% (95%CI: 67.6-77.9) were amyloid-positive, and 49.7% (95%CI: 44.0-55.5) remained eligible after applying safety criteria. Overall, 9.7% (95%CI: 8.6-10.8) of patients consulting memory clinics were estimated to be eligible for lecanemab, representing approximately 18,200 individuals nationally (annual average, 2022-2024). These results inform healthcare planning for disease-modifying therapy implementation in France and comparable countries.

title: Personalising Deformable Image Registration with Clinical Context and Deformation History for Adaptive Radiotherapy
abstract: Adaptive radiotherapy must account for anatomical changes during treatment, but doing so depends on reliably mapping targets, organs at risk and dose across serial images. Existing registration methods treat each image pair independently, without using radiotherapy-specific context or the patient's preceding anatomical trajectory. We developed Clinical-context-Aware and Patient-adaptive Deformable Image Registration (CAP-DIR), integrating source contours, dose, clinical text and prior-registration features. We evaluated 16,361 CT examinations from 3,473 patients across four institutional cohorts and five public benchmarks. CAP-DIR increased internal-test organ-at-risk-region normalized cross-correlation from 84.76% to 96.92% relative to the strongest learning-based comparator, with low deformation folding, and remained superior across seven external cohorts. In a blinded review of 20 longitudinal cases, clinically acceptable contours increased from 45.0% to 82.5% for clinical target volumes and from 22.5% to 62.5% for organs at risk, while estimated editing time decreased. In a controlled benchmark, CAP-DIR reduced global dose-mapping error by 34.5% relative to the strongest comparator. These findings show that clinically informed, longitudinal registration can improve contour usability and dose mapping for adaptive radiotherapy.

title: Using Generative Artificial Intelligence to Craft Patient-Facing Report Summaries: Opportunities for Enhancing Resident Training
abstract: IntroductionEffective patient communication is an essential skill for radiology and nuclear medicine specialists, yet it remains underemphasized in residency training. With increasing patient access to electronic medical records, the ability to translate technical reports into patient-facing summaries is critical. Generative AI may offer a dual benefit of improving workflow by producing patient-appropriate summaries and serving as a training tool to help residents hone their communication skills. MethodsSeventy-six de-identified nuclear medicine imaging procedure reports (covering general nuclear medicine, PET/CT (positron emission tomography-computed tomography), and nuclear cardiology) were used to generate 608 patient-facing summaries: four versions of each report were generated using ChatGPT models (o1-mini, 4o, 4o-mini, 4 legacy) and four versions were written by residents. Summaries adhered to a four-sentence maximum and targeted a sixth-grade reading level. GPT-4o was used to critique and rank AI-generated summaries, and the two best-performing AI versions were compared with resident summaries. Blinded evaluations by three experienced nuclear medicine physicians assessed summaries on readability, accuracy, appropriateness, and overall fitness for purpose. Likelihood Ratio Chi-Square tests assessed differences in performance. ResultsGPT o1-mini was ranked as the best summary in 86% of initial AI comparisons and 100% of final comparative assessments with resident summaries. GPT 4o and o1-mini outperformed residents across multiple domains including clarity, health literacy, and tone. The best human summaries were consistently outperformed by AI in both physician and AI assessments, though discrepancies in ranking priorities (e.g., tolerance for jargon vs. inaccuracy) were noted and AI more often produced summaries containing misinterpretations of data in the original reports. Resident summaries showed wide variation in tone, technicality, and patient appropriateness. Overall, 65% of all summaries (AI and human) were deemed fit-for-purpose. ConclusionGenerative AI models can produce consistently appropriate and readable patient-facing summaries of imaging procedure reports and may serve as effective tools to develop resident communication skills. Generative AI may therefore model best practices and provide timely feedback, offering structured opportunities to refine written communication. Future work should explore its integration into learner-tailored educational constructs using frameworks such as Bloom’s taxonomy, to enhance resident training and effectiveness of feedback mechanisms.

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Medical Diagnosis: A Modality-Wise Review of Clinical Records, Biosignals and Medical Images
abstract: Machine learning now supports diagnosis in many clinical settings, from risk scores built on patient records to deep networks that read scans. The evidence, however, is split by data type. Studies on tabular records, biosignals and medical images use different models, different metrics and different validation practices, so it is hard to judge which approach suits a new diagnostic task. This paper reviews diagnostic learning across three data modalities: structured clinical and screening records, physiological signals collected by sensors and IoT devices, and medical images such as CT, MRI, X-ray, echocardiography and dermoscopy. It links each modality to the models that are reported to work best on it and to the practical problems that come with it. The review finds that feature selection combined with tree ensembles or hybrid classifiers performs well on structured records, that random forests and support vector machines remain strong on extracted signal features, and that convolutional networks and their ensembles lead on images. Across all three modalities, class imbalance, small single-centre datasets and limited explanation are recurring problems, and privacy rules restrict the pooling of data. Future work should report recall and calibration next to accuracy, test models on external sites, and adopt privacy-preserving training such as federated continual learning.

title: SPELUNKA: A Framework for Finding Unanticipated Associations in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are the backbone of many state-of-the-art multimodal systems, but often encode spurious and harmful associations from their training data. While prior work focuses on removing known biases from VLMs, methods for discovering unanticipated associations for retrieval tasks remain underexplored. We introduce SPELUNKA, an automated, inference-time framework for finding unanticipated distributional biases for retrieval tasks in VLMs without pre-specified labeled subgroups, inference-time human supervision, or model fine-tuning. Given a concept of interest, SPELUNKA generates captions for related images, extracts relevant entities from captions, and selects semantically meaningful associations. A frequency-based detection rule then identifies spurious associations by measuring over- or under-representation of these attributes in a VLM's top-ranked outputs relative to their full dataset distribution. We evaluate SPELUNKA across four datasets, and find that it 1) successfully recovers both synthetic and naturally occurring spurious correlations, 2) achieves an average AUROC of 0.93 across four datasets in identifying images strongly associated with a query, and 3) outperforms baselines in finding features that are strongly associated with a given query.

title: Optimizing AI-assisted decision-making in mammography screening: focusing on uncertainties
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate an AI-based decision-support system for mammography interpretation, assessing its impact on diagnostic performance. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 130,838 mammograms from 35,709 patients with confirmed follow-up outcomes across multiple centers, using the Digital Database for Screening Mammography (DDSM) for external validation. Representing one of the largest datasets from the Middle East, it evaluates model generalizability in underrepresented populations. An AI super-model incorporated separate UNet-based networks for lesion segmentation, a high-resolution model (4096) for calcifications, a multi-resolution ensemble (4096, 2048, 1024) for macro-scale lesions, and a risk-assessment model for malignancy prediction. Radiologists interpreted images under five scenarios: unaided, AI-assisted, AI as the final decision-maker in uncertain cases, union of radiologist and AI decisions in uncertain cases, and standalone AI. RESULTS: AI assistance significantly enhanced performance across all scenarios. Based on aggregated reader performance, AUC improved from 83.04% (95% CI: 79.8-86.3) unaided to 88.40% (95% CI: 85.6-91.2) in the union scenario (p < 0.001). Sensitivity increased from 54.8% (95% CI: 48.6-61.0) to 83.9% (95% CI: 79.3-88.4) (p < 0.001), and specificity rose from 83.6% (95% CI: 82.0-85.3) to 91.1% (95% CI: 89.8-92.4) (p < 0.001). Multi-resolution segmentation effectively detected calcifications and challenging lesions. DDSM validation confirmed model robustness. AI showed particular promise in aiding less-experienced radiologists in underserved areas to improve early cancer detection. CONCLUSIONS: AI in mammography interpretation improves diagnostic accuracy and reduces uncertainty, supporting early breast cancer detection and optimized screening workflows. KEY POINTS: Question Can an AI-based decision-support system improve the accuracy of mammography interpretation, reduce diagnostic uncertainty, and support less-experienced radiologists? Findings In this retrospective multicenter study, AI-assisted mammography improved sensitivity and specificity, increased cancer detection, and reduced recalls and false positives. Critical relevance statement AI integration in mammography enhances diagnostic accuracy, reduces unnecessary recalls, and supports more confident and efficient clinical decision-making, particularly by improving the performance of less-experienced radiologists in underserved and resource-limited settings where expert interpretation may be limited.

title: PlanPath: Exploration-Guided Orchestration for Patient-Level Pathology Reasoning
abstract: A patient's pathology case spans tens of slides from distinct specimens and anatomical sites, each carrying non-redundant, site-specific evidence. Forming a patient-level conclusion therefore requires locating the slides relevant to a given question and integrating complementary findings across them. However, existing pathology agents analyze one slide at a time and describe morphology rather than measure it, leaving evidence acquisition across a patient's specimens and patient-level quantification underexplored. To address this gap, we propose PlanPath, an agentic framework for patient-level pathology visual question answering (VQA). PlanPath turns the question into an exploration plan that specifies the evidence required, routes to the slides likely to carry it, and drives coarse-to-fine acquisition from tissue architecture down to individual cells. Tissue- and cell-level tools supply the counts, proportions, and extents, which PlanPath aggregates across slides into a traceable answer. To enable evaluation, we build two patient-level VQA datasets for renal and gastric cancer, averaging 15 WSIs per patient, with pathologist-verified question-answer pairs derived from diagnostic reports. Experimental results show that PlanPath outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.4% and 12.1% in overall accuracy on the two datasets and further improves existing slide-level agents when plugged into our framework. The dataset and code are available at: https://github.com/JSGe-AI/PlanPath_1.

title: A multiview video–text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography
abstract: Invasive coronary angiography is the reference standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, yet assessment is subjective, and existing artificial-intelligence tools typically assess stenosis in individual frames or videos and do not integrate the full multiview angiographic study. Here we show that DeepCORO-CLIP, trained on 203,808 angiographic videos and reports from 28,117 patients, interprets whole multiple-video angiograms at once. It detects obstructive stenoses (≥70%), with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.89 internally and externally, and identifies chronic total occlusion (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.95), intra-coronary thrombus and calcification (AUROC = 0.90 to 0.91). It also predicts 1-year cardiovascular events (AUROC = 0.79, 95% CI of 0.74 to 0.84, versus 0.65 for a model derived using clinical variables) and left ventricular ejection fraction (mean absolute error 7.3% versus 8.8% for a previous model), both achieved using coronary angiography alone. In a blinded review of 365 evaluations across 288 angiograms, its reports were clinically usable in 76% of evaluations versus 88% for cardiologists, with comparable false positives (17% versus 14%, P = 0.38); residual missed stenoses reflected an adjustable threshold rather than an absent signal.

title: Beyond the Image: Inferring Latent Signature Dynamics with DynaSigNet for Robust Writer Identification
abstract: Signature-based writer identification from static images is a critical biometric task, yet it traditionally ignores the rich, dynamic information of the signing process. This paper introduces DynaSigNet (Dynamic Signature Network), a novel deep learning framework that overcomes this limitation by learning to infer the latent generative dynamics—trajectory, velocity, and pressure—from a single offline signature. Our architecture employs a synergistic CNN-Transformer backbone to produce a holistic feature representation that captures both local textures and global structural dependencies. The core of our method is a multi-task learning paradigm where this shared representation is decoded in parallel: a primary head for writer classification, and auxiliary motor-imagination heads for predicting the dynamic properties. By training the model to understand how the signature was formed, we achieve a more discriminative feature space. Validated on a challenging bilingual dataset of Roman and Bengali scripts, DynaSigNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating that inferring latent motor processes is a powerful new direction for static biometric analysis. A system graphical user interface (GUI) is also implemented.

title: Automated segmentation and clinical characterization of layered plaque in intracoronary optical coherence tomography
abstract: Background Layered plaque, representing organized thrombus overlying a previously disrupted plaque, is a marker of coronary destabilization and plaque vulnerability. Despite its clinical relevance, identifying layered plaque remains expert dependent with interobserver variability, limiting large-scale assessment. We developed and validated an artificial intelligence (AI) model for layered plaque segmentation, and assessed occurrence and associations with plaque vulnerability in non-culprit lesions. Methods Optical coherence tomography (OCT) pullbacks from the PECTUS-obs and ORANGE datasets were used to develop an enhanced version of our validated multiclass segmentation model (OCT-AID), by adding layered plaque as an additional pixel-level class. Pullbacks were divided into a training set ( n = 4121 frames, 493 with layered plaque) and an independent held-out test set ( n = 433 frames, 71 with layered plaque). Using this model, prevalence of layered plaque and associations with plaque vulnerability features were studied in patients with non-culprit lesions (PECTUS-obs data; 414 patients, 488 lesions). Results The model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.68 ± 0.27 for layered plaque segmentation, with pullback-level sensitivity of 96.2% and specificity of 75.0%. At least one layered plaque was present in 366/414 patients (88.4%). Presence of layered plaque was higher in STEMI patients ( p = 0.018) . Lesions containing layered plaques showed higher prevalence of lipid-rich plaque (76.4% vs. 60.9%, p = 0.008 ), thin-cap fibroatheroma (29.2% vs. 15.6%, p = 0.016 ), macrophage accumulation (25.0% vs 9.4%, p = 0.010 ), and cholesterol clefts (0.0% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.009 ). Conclusions Automated OCT-based identification of layered plaque using AI is feasible. In non-culprit coronary lesions, layered plaque was highly prevalent and associated with established markers of plaque vulnerability.

title: Reliability of large language models for clinical data extraction in AI decision support tools
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have significant potential in healthcare, such as automating routine tasks and supporting complex decision-making processes. In fields like oncology, LLMs can extract and organize unstructured patient data, streamlining workflows and supporting imaging or clinical evaluations. This information can then be integrated into predictive models, enhancing patient prognosis assessments. However, deploying LLMs poses challenges, some of which are related to their performance variability due to the inherent probabilistic nature of LLMs, prompt differences, and software updates, which may lead to inconsistent outcomes. Even with identical prompts and contexts, LLMs can exhibit variability. It is essential to rigorously evaluate the clinical accuracy and reproducible outcomes of the LLM for clinical data extraction in clinical settings for AI decision support tools and clinical use. Reliable information retrieval requires consistent LLM behavior. The study of the LLMs variability and its effect on clinical AI decision support tools will be presented and discussed.

title: Establishing standardized evaluation protocols for peptide-target interaction prediction: the PTI-TAPE consensus framework eDelphi
abstract: Computational peptide-target interaction (PTI) prediction has advanced rapidly as a tool for drug discovery, yet the field lacks agreed evaluation standards. Discrepancies in metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction across publications currently render cross-study comparisons methodologically intractable, ultimately impeding the clinical translation of therapeutic peptides. To resolve this, we present PTI-TAPE (Peptide-Target Interaction-Tasks Assessing Peptide Engagement), a standardised benchmarking framework developed via a structured three-round eDelphi consensus study with 15 international experts spanning computational biology, machine learning, and regulatory science. Operating under a robust consensus threshold (>80% agreement), the panel established 26 definitive standards across eight domains, governed by the new STRIDE (Standardisation, Transparency, Representativeness, Integration, Discovery, Evidence) framework. Key outcomes include mandating specific primary metrics for affinity and structure, enforcing a tiered negative sampling hierarchy that prioritizes experimental non-binders, and requiring mandatory temporal dataset splits. By providing a unified reporting checklist, benchmark specifications, and a biennial governance structure, PTI-TAPE ensures reproducible evaluation and fair method comparison, bridging the gap between computational PTI predictions and genuine therapeutic benefit.

title: The relationship between potential categories of self-management behavior and disease knowledge level of gout patients based on K-means clustering analysis
abstract: Objective To explore the potential categories of self-management behaviors of gout patients, analyze the relationship between each category and the disease knowledge level, and provide a basis for formulating targeted intervention strategies. Methods A total of 402 patients with gout were selected by convenience sampling. The general information questionnaire, the gout patients’ self-management assessment scale, and the knowledge level measurement questionnaire were used in this study. K-means cluster analysis was used to identify the potential categories of self-management behavior. Results The score of self-management behavior of gout patients was (142.30 ± 29.53), which could be divided into four categories: high self-management-knowledge adequacy type (28.6%), low self-management-knowledge deficiency type (15.4%), moderate self-management-insufficient transformation type (30.8%), and good self-management-knowledge deficiency type (25.1%). There were statistically significant differences in age, residence, number of acute flares in the past year, serum uric acid (SUA) level and disease knowledge level among different categories ( p < 0.05). Conclusion There is heterogeneity in self-management behavior of gout patients, and there are differences in disease knowledge level among different types of patients. Medical staff should implement hierarchical and precise intervention based on category characteristics.

title: Images Talk Back: Guiding MMDiTs by Suppressing Image-to-Text Feedback
abstract: Multimodal diffusion transformers (MMDiTs) allow the evolving image to update internal text representations through joint attention. These representations then guide subsequent image updates, raising a question: does this feedback help correct deviations from the prompt, or preserve them? We find that image-to-text (I2T) feedback can preserve the objects and attributes already represented in the evolving image, including errors. Transplanting I2T messages can rescue failures or disrupt successes. At matched intervention strengths, suppressing the influence of I2T feedback improves generation, whereas opposite controls degrade it. These findings motivate Semantic Feedback Guidance (SFG), which suppresses the influence of I2T feedback by guiding away from an auxiliary branch that strengthens this feedback and weakens text-to-image conditioning. The in-place variant, iSFG, directly suppresses I2T feedback and strengthens text-to-image conditioning, requiring no extra model evaluations. Temporal interventions motivate running the SFG branch during the first 20% of image sampling steps, requiring about $1.2\times$ the base NFE without classifier-free guidance (CFG). Experiments across three image-generation backbones show gains in alignment and preference-model scores. On FLUX, adding SFG to CFG raises GenEval from $0.6661$ to $0.7479$; on SD3.5M, iSFG adds $+1.33$ HPSv2.1 over CFG at zero extra NFE. The control also transfers to text-to-video and image-to-video generation, improving VBench scores. Code is available at https://github.com/yyc1215lll-creator/SFG.

title: OpenMSK: A modular open-source framework for comprehensive analysis of imaging biomarkers in knee osteoarthritis
abstract: Objective To develop and validate a fully automated, extendable, open-source AI-driven pipeline capable of knee magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation and quantitative extraction of MRI and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging biomarkers. Design For model training, open-source knee MRI data from 347 knees acquired across 7 scanners using multiple gradient-echo sequences were used. An independent test set of 20 knees from 3T PET-MRI examinations were used for evaluation in this prospective reliability and agreement study. The pipeline segmented femoral, tibial, and patellar bones and cartilage, and medial and lateral menisci using three different deep learning models. Quantitative outputs included cartilage thickness and T 2 relaxation times, meniscus volume and T 2 ∗ relaxation times, bone shape scores, and static and kinetic subchondral bone PET measures. Manual segmentations from two annotators served as reference standards. Segmentation performance was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients (DSC), average symmetric surface distances, and volume differences. Quantitative outcome agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Pearson correlations, and root mean square error. Results Automated segmentations demonstrated high spatial agreement with manual annotations, with DSCs ranging from 0.84 to 0.98 across all tissues. Quantitative PET-MRI biomarkers generally demonstrated high agreement, although confidence intervals were wide for several biomarkers. Conclusion OpenMSK enables multi-tissue knee segmentation and generation of quantitative MRI and PET biomarkers, with performance assessed against two independent annotators and across different U-Net-based segmentation architectures. As a freely available, modular platform, OpenMSK lowers technical barriers to whole-joint quantitative imaging and provides a standardized foundation for OA research and clinical translation.

title: Spatiotemporal Mapping of Glomerular Endothelial Regeneration Identifies Apold1 as an Intrinsic Regulator of Repair
abstract: Abstract Endothelial cell (EC) injury is central to the pathogenesis of various renal disorders, highlighting the critical importance of vascular repair for restoring organ health. However, due to limited access to human tissue during active regeneration, the exact reparative processes remain largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate regeneration mechanisms specifically within the glomerular microvasculature by utilizing a selective endothelial cell injury (ECI) model in mice. Lineage tracing identified the origin of regenerating ECs. To uncover the transcriptional dynamics driving these reparative changes, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing and Xenium spatial transcriptomics (ST), mapping distinct glomerular EC (gEC) subpopulations across different phases of injury and recovery. Apold1 emerged as a key regulatory candidate within this process. To functionally validate this gene’s specific role during the regenerative phase, Apold1-deficient (Apold1-/-) mice underwent the ECI model. After showing that gECs regenerate primarily from local, pre-existing renal ECs, our transcriptomic analysis identified 10 distinct gEC subpopulations and revealed a complex temporal pattern of regeneration. This process begins with the expression of genes associated with inflammation, followed sequentially by endothelial cell (EC) migration, the activation of immediate early genes, vascular remodeling and cellular proliferation. Within this dynamic process, the EC-specific gene Apold1 was identified as a key regulatory candidate. Apold1 -/- mice exhibited impaired endothelial regeneration, characterized by increased endothelial activation and greater immune cell infiltration seven days post-ECI. To our knowledge, this is the first study to elucidate the spatiotemporal mechanisms of glomerular endothelial cell regeneration. By identifying local gECs as the primary source of repair, and stablishing the change in their expression pattern during regeneration, as well as identifying Apold1 as an intrinsic regulator, we have laid the groundwork for future research on renal microvascular disorders. Translational Statement Using EC-lineage-tracing mice and transcriptomic-techniques, we identified new endothelial subpopulations that drive injury and regeneration post-ECI. We provide insights into the local processes that orchestrate gEC regeneration and highlight complex gene patterns with several newly identified targets in renal endothelial regeneration (e.g. immediate early genes and Apold1 ). These results hold strong potential for clinical translation stimulating the development of cell therapies or other strategies to support the physiological endothelial regeneration. We functionally validate the gene Apold1 in the process of gEC regeneration. Future steps include thoroughly characterizing the influence of Apold1 during endothelial regeneration in mice and humans, and exploring its clinical application to improve endothelial recovery in microvascular renal diseases.
